title: Square-zero extension data and normalized ring maps on algebraic-space charts
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale ringed sites [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use sheaves of modules as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $g:X\to Y$ and ring presheaves $A,D$ on $Y_{\mathrm{et}},X_{\mathrm{et}}$, respectively, a chart ring map consists of unital ring maps $A(V)\to D(U)$ for every commuting square of scheme charts $U\to X$, $V\to Y$, $a:U\to V$ over $g$, natural in every commuting square between two such pairs of charts. On sheaves these are the $g$-maps describing maps $g^{-1}A\to D$. A space first-order thickening $i:X\to X'$ means a representable map whose base change to any scheme is a first-order thickening of schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. A normalized site model for $i$ consists of an equivalence $E:X'_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{et}}$, continuous in both directions, and natural scheme reduction arrows $U\to E^{-1}U$ over $S$ exhibiting $U=X\times_{X'}E^{-1}U$. Its transported ring presheaf is $R_i(U)=\Gamma(E^{-1}U,\mathcal O)$, with quotient $p_i:R_i\to\mathcal O_X$ the pullback of regular functions along these reduction arrows. For $f:X\to B$ and $q:X'\to B$, a normalized model over $B$ additionally has a chart ring map $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B\to R_i$: for every reduced chart square $a:U\to V$ it is prescribed by an actual lift $a':E^{-1}U\to V$ over $q$ with $a'|_U=a$, as pullback of regular functions. No existence of such models is asserted here.

For a module $G$ on $X$ and $f:X\to B$, square-zero extension data consist of a sheaf of commutative unital rings $A$, a ring-sheaf map $p:A\to\mathcal O_X$, an additive sheaf map $j:G\to A$, and a chart ring map $\beta:f^{-1}\mathcal O_B\to A$. Require $j$ injective on every object, $\ker p(U)=j(G(U))$ on every object, and $p$ locally surjective: every section of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ lifts after restriction to a covering sieve of $U$. Require $j(m)j(n)=0$ and $j(p(a)m)=a j(m)$ for every object and its sections. Require $p\beta=f^\sharp$, whose component at a chart square $a:U\to V$ is pullback of regular functions along $a$. Thus the kernel has its prescribed quotient module action, without requiring sectionwise surjectivity.

For normalized models of $i:X\to X'$ and $j:Y\to Y'$, a chart ring map $\alpha:g^{-1}R_j\to R_i$ reduces to $g^\sharp$ when its composite with $p_i$ equals $g^\sharp g^{-1}p_j$ on every chart pair. For models over $B$ it is over the base when $\beta_j(b)\alpha(a)=\beta_i(ba)$ on every composable triple of charts. It is induced by $g':X'\to Y'$ when each reduced chart square $a:U\to V$ has a scheme lift $a':E_i^{-1}U\to E_j^{-1}V$ commuting with $g'$ and reduction, and its regular-function pullback is the prescribed component of $\alpha$. For two models on the same reduced $X$, a specified ring-presheaf isomorphism $\theta:R_j\simeq R_i$ is induced by an isomorphism $e:X'\simeq Y'$ when for every $U$ the corresponding two lifted charts admit a map over $e$, commuting with their reduction maps, whose regular-function pullback is $\theta_U$. These are predicates only, with no existence or uniqueness assertion.
